channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [9] Light-induced asymmetric pseudogap below the critical temperature in cuprates
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: A. J. Millis, F. Boschini

Authors: D. Armanno, O. Gingras, F. Goto, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct relevance to time-resolved photoemission and unconventional superconductivity.

Tags: #ARPES #cuprate #superconductivity

Abstract: How superconductivity relates to the pseudogap in cuprates remains unclear. Now, time-resolved photoemission measurements show a light-induced pseudogap-like state below critical temperature, revealing a dynamic interplay with superconductivity.

item.title: [7] Evidence for spin-fluctuation-mediated superconductivity in electron-doped cuprates
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: K. Jin, N. E. Hussey

Authors: C. M. Duffy, S. J. Tu, Q. H. Chen, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Important research on mechanism of superconductivity in cuprates.

Tags: #superconductivity #cuprate

Abstract: The mechanism for superconductivity in cuprates is still not known. Now, the observation of a relationship between the critical temperature and strength of coupling between electrons and spin fluctuations suggests the latter as a prime candidate.
